note: One build over the shared errata source: each register carries one replaced claim, and each projection is scoped to its register (states by `register`, entry issues by locator, output issues by subject) and names the claim in its `note`. The register `conflict` carries no errata here; its refusal is errata-column-edition-bindings-fail-the-build step 2. The replaced tests asserted entry codes and compiled effects; values beyond them are derived, not copied: the blocker tokens in `detail` are `convert_delivered_entry`'s blocker vocabulary (the strings the errata-delivered-components-* cases pin), and the output issues (missing_coding_period, unsupported_occurrence, no_supported_states, unresolved_flag) are the boundary consequences of the old claims: no coding on the additions, an unknown edition scope, an unset sensitivity. The blanks state_codes row also restates test_source_effects.py::test_added_occurrence_copies_coding_only_with_explicit_checked_declaration's first claim: an addition that declares no coding copy gets no coding although its evidence rows carry a list (`coding_records == ()`); the declared-copy half is matrix-blank-answers-inherit-the-donor-code-list.
fails_if: any one of, per register: `compile_errata` counts every native edition of a variant named by `[[identity.edition_split]]` as moved (split), or stops refusing an addition to a moved edition (moved); `convert_delivered_entry` drops the no_documented_column_identity, ambiguous_documented_column_identity or now_present blocker (nodoc, twovars, present); the delivered-blank rebinding accepts several split owners of the literal column, or leaves an unowned literal unsplit in a split family (owners, unowned); an errata addition takes its coding from its evidence rows, so the 2022 addition inherits the donor's list (blanks); a holdings_period column gets an unpooled interval scope (columns); scb-docs defaults an omitted flag to false (declared); or the coding peers `compile_coding_register` digests leave out the blank rows pooled in by `[[errata.delivered]]` (pooled, twocols)
